name: GD25Q80 program flash
desc: 1 MB SPI NOR flash behind the HR_C7000 LCSFC, mapped for execute-in-place at 0x03000000 (flash offset = address - 0x03000000). Layout seen in the stock image: 0x000000 DH_FLAG boot header (0x0c646874, load address 0x03001000, check word 0x0f647874) in a sector that is otherwise mostly zeros; 0x001000 boot entry, whose code includes the YMODEM upgrade loader (0x03004618) and a jump to the application at 0x0300c000 (0x030017fc); 0x00b000 one 4 KB per-unit settings sector, rewritten by the firmware; 0x00c000-0x0fffff application (the range the upgrade loader erases). Never erase 0x000000-0x00bfff without a verified full backup of the same radio.

blocks.name: Status register
blocks.desc: One 16-bit register S15-S0, read as two bytes: 05h returns S7-S0, 35h returns S15-S8. Written only by 01h with one byte (S7-S0; CS rising after 8 bits CLEARS CMP and QE) or two bytes (S7-S0, S15-S8). No 31h on this part. 50h before 01h writes volatile copies. Reserved bits S11-S12 omitted. The datasheet labels opcode 35h 'Read Status Register-1'; this file calls the bytes SR1 (S7-S0) and SR2 (S15-S8) to match the W25Q128JV description.

blocks.name: Identification
blocks.desc: The datasheet's feature list also promises a 128-bit unique ID and four 256-byte security registers (44h/42h/48h, A15-A8 = 00h-03h), but documents no opcode for reading the unique ID; neither is described here.
blocks.ds_ref: GD25Q80C Rev 1.0, 1, PDF p.4; Table of ID Definitions, PDF p.14

blocks.name: Instruction set
blocks.desc: One pseudo-register per opcode at offset = opcode. A = 3 address bytes. Program, erase and status-write commands need a preceding 06h and must end on a byte boundary.

registers.name: Status Register S7-S0
registers.desc: Read with 05h (wire_addr), written with wr_cmd. Delivered as 0x00.
registers.ds_ref: GD25Q80C Rev 1.0, 6, PDF p.10; initial delivery state 8.2, PDF p.41
registers.fw_writes: 0x0002bb98: 01h at 0x0002bbe8, first data byte 0x00 (0x0002bbf0), only when 35h showed QE = 0.
registers.fw_reads: 0x0002bb98 (raw SSI 0x04000000): after the 01h write, polls 05h (sent at 0x0002bc0e) until the whole byte reads 0x00.

fields.name: WIP
fields.desc: Write in progress. Status only.
fields.fw_reads: 0x0002bb98 waits for the whole byte to be 0, which includes WIP. The LCSFC path never reads it (see file header).

fields.name: WEL
fields.desc: Write enable latch. Status only.

fields.name: BP
fields.desc: Block protect BP4:BP0 (S6:S2), non-volatile; with CMP selects the protected area (Table 1.0/1.1). Chip erase runs only when BP2:BP0 = 0 and CMP = 0.
fields.ds_ref: GD25Q80C Rev 1.0, 6, PDF p.10; Table 1.0-1.1, PDF p.8-9
fields.fw_writes: 0x0002bb98 writes 0 (via the 0x00 first byte of 01h) when it sets QE.

fields.name: SRP0
fields.desc: Status register protect 0 (with SRP1 and WP#: software / hardware / power-supply lock-down / OTP). Non-volatile.

registers.name: Status Register S15-S8
registers.desc: Read with 35h (wire_addr), written with wr_cmd. Delivered as 0x00.
registers.wr_cmd: 01h (second data byte; a one-byte 01h clears CMP and QE), after 06h or 50h. No 31h on this part
registers.ds_ref: GD25Q80C Rev 1.0, 6, PDF p.10-11; initial delivery state 8.2, PDF p.41
registers.fw_writes: 0x0002bb98: second data byte of 01h = 0x02 (0x0002bbf8), i.e. QE = 1 and SRP1 = LB = HPF = CMP = SUS = 0.
registers.fw_reads: 0x0002bb98 (raw SSI 0x04000000): 35h at 0x0002bbb0, reads one byte, tests bit 1 (QE, andi 2 at 0x0002bbc2).

fields.name: SRP1
fields.desc: Status register protect 1. Non-volatile.

fields.name: QE
fields.desc: Quad enable. Non-volatile; default 0. Must be 1 for the LCSFC's quad XIP (SystemControl QUAD_ENABLE).
fields.fw_writes: 0x0002bb98 sets it to 1 (01h 00h 02h) when found 0, then writes 0x01000001 to SystemControl QUAD_ENABLE 0x1100005c. Reached from 0x0002e158, called from 0x0300c074.

fields.name: LB
fields.desc: Security register lock (OTP: once 1, the security registers are read-only forever). Default 0.

fields.name: HPF
fields.desc: High performance flag (set while in A3h high-performance mode). Status only. Labelled HPM in the bit figure, HPF in the text.

fields.name: CMP
fields.desc: Complement protect, with BP4:BP0. Non-volatile; default 0. Cleared by a one-byte 01h.
fields.ds_ref: GD25Q80C Rev 1.0, 6, PDF p.11; 7.4, PDF p.16

fields.name: SUS
fields.desc: Program/erase suspended (75h sets, 7Ah or power cycle clears). Status only.

registers.name: JEDEC ID
registers.desc: Returned by 9Fh, manufacturer first. Not read on a radio; the stock firmware never sends 9Fh to this chip.
registers.ds_ref: GD25Q80C Rev 1.0, Table of ID Definitions, PDF p.14; 7.23, PDF p.30

fields.name: CAPACITY
fields.desc: Capacity ID7-ID0 (14h = 8 Mbit).

fields.name: MEMORY_TYPE
fields.desc: Memory type ID15-ID8 (40h).

fields.name: MF
fields.desc: Manufacturer ID (GigaDevice = C8h).

registers.name: Write Status Register (WRSR)
registers.desc: Frame: 06h, then 01h S7-S0 [S15-S8]. A one-byte write clears CMP and QE. Can set the OTP LB bit and the SRP1:SRP0 = 11 OTP lock.
registers.fw_writes: Raw SSI only: 0x0002bb98 sends 01h (0x0002bbe8) 00h (0x0002bbf0) 02h (0x0002bbf8) after 06h, only when 35h shows QE = 0. The only status-register write in the stock firmware, to either flash chip.

fields.name: Opcode
fields.desc: Command byte, shifted in MSB first after CS# falls. The stock firmware forms this value (as a stored byte or the top byte of a stored word on the LCSFC path, or as an SSI data byte); see the register's fw_writes.

registers.name: Page Program (PP)
registers.desc: Frame: 06h, then 02h A D1..D256 within one 256-byte page.
registers.fw_writes: LCSFC path, issued only by 0x0002bca4 (word (02h<<24|addr) to 0x03800000 at 0x0002bce4, data to 0x03800000, last byte to 0x03000000 at 0x0002bd12), built in 0x0002beb8 (bseti 25 at 0x0002bf1e, preceded by 06h). Callers of 0x0002beb8: flash_cache_sector_modify_and_writeback 0x0301ca44 (0x0301cab4, rewrites the 4 KB settings sector 0x00b000, retrying until it succeeds); FUN_0002c0f8 (0x0002c148, restores 4 bytes at 0x00b10c) and FUN_0002c160 (0x0002c19a, 0x00b000 + offset), both called from the CPS loops serial_protocol_vframe_command_loop 0x0302a044 (0x0302a17c/0x0302a186) and its variant 0x0302a4dc (0x0302a690/0x0302a69a). Direct stores (not via 0x0002bca4): the boot-header repair 0x0002bd20 programs the 12-byte header at 0x000000 (0x0002bd62-0x0002bd74) when the header check fails. Bootloader twins: flash_region_write_chunked 0x03003f60 via 0x03003d5c (0x03003d9c), called by 0x0300407c (renamed 2026-10-11 from locked_integer_increment_with_fail_flag to ymodem_flash_block_program; it programs a received YMODEM block) from xmodem_ymodem_block_receive_loop 0x03004618 (0x030047e0); header programming in 0x03003dd0 (0x03003e12).

fields.name: Opcode
fields.desc: Command byte, shifted in MSB first after CS# falls. The stock firmware forms this value (as a stored byte or the top byte of a stored word on the LCSFC path, or as an SSI data byte); see the register's fw_writes.

registers.name: Read Data
registers.fw_writes: Not sent by firmware code; reads go through LCSFC execute-in-place (which read opcode the LCSFC uses is not documented).

fields.name: Opcode
fields.desc: Command byte, shifted in MSB first after CS# falls.

registers.name: Write Disable (WRDI)
registers.fw_writes: LCSFC path: byte 0x04 stored to 0x03000000 unconditionally at the start of the boot-header check 0x0002bd20 (0x0002bd28; reached at every boot via 0x0002bf80 from radio_boot_full_init_sequence 0x0305f304), and in its bootloader twin 0x03003dd0 (0x03003dd8). 0x0002bca4 also has a 04h branch (0x0002bcc0) that no caller uses.

registers.name: Read Status Register S7-S0
registers.fw_writes: Raw SSI only: 0x0002bc0e in the poll loop of 0x0002bb98. Not used on the LCSFC path (0x0002bc78 / 0x03003d30 re-read the boot header through XIP instead).

registers.name: Write Enable (WREN)
registers.fw_writes: LCSFC path: byte 0x06 stored to 0x03000000 at 0x0002bcb2 (0x0002bca4, mode 1), called before every erase (0x0002be2c in 0x0002bde8) and program (0x0002bf12 in 0x0002beb8); also at 0x0002bd48 and 0x0002bd58 in the boot-header repair 0x0002bd20. Bootloader twins: 0x03003d6a (0x03003d5c), 0x03003df8 and 0x03003e08 (flash_controller_descriptor_init_once 0x03003dd0). Raw SSI: 0x0002bbd4 in 0x0002bb98.

registers.name: Sector Erase (SE)
registers.desc: Frame: 06h, then 20h A. Erases one 4 KB sector.
registers.fw_writes: LCSFC path, issued by 0x0002bca4 (word (20h<<24|addr) to 0x03000000 at 0x0002bcd4), built per 4 KB sector in 0x0002bde8 (bseti 29 at 0x0002be0e; 06h first). Callers of 0x0002bde8: flash_cache_sector_modify_and_writeback 0x0301ca44 (0x0301ca92, sector 0x00b000; spins forever at 0x0301ca9a if the erase reports failure) and FUN_0002c0f8 (0x0002c11e, sector 0x00b000; CPS path from 0x0302a17c and 0x0302a690). Direct store 0x20000000 (sector 0x000000, the boot header) at 0x0002bd4e in 0x0002bd20, executed at every boot (0x0002bf80 <- radio_boot_full_init_sequence 0x0305f304) but only when the header word is not 0x0c646874 or word 2 != word 1 + 0x0c646874. Bootloader twins: flash_sector_erase_range_4kb 0x03003e9c via 0x03003d5c (0x03003d8c), called by FUN_03004040 (0x03004060) which erases every sector 0x00c000-0x0fffff (the whole application) from xmodem_ymodem_block_receive_loop (0x03004762); header-sector erase in flash_controller_descriptor_init_once 0x03003dd0 (0x03003dfe), whose only caller FUN_03004030 has no direct caller.
